answer: Recursive ring detection with compounding bonds. From a flagged account, walk attestations outward in a spiral, freezing each account a ring touches until it closes or exits into honest graph. Ring members forfeit bonds; each detection raises the cluster bond multiplier, so repeat-farm costs spiral. Reputation moves at glacier pace, unlocked per epoch served, so an aged account is a juniper: slow-grown, distinct in timing and wording from farm output. Weakness: operators sacrifice one cheap ring to cut off the walk; pay detectors per confirmed ring, not per frozen account.
